title: Patron and Doctor
hook: why would the patron of missions be a nun who never left her convent?
tomorrow: so what is her little way, really? and is it easy?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Thérèse's last words, said after months of darkness: my God, I love you. That was your line. Today, what the Church did with her story afterward.
screen: `MY GOD, I LOVE YOU.` → `WHAT CAME AFTER.`

segments.voice: Some titles don't seem to match the résumé. A travel account run by someone who's never left her hometown. A cooking star who can't boil an egg. The Catholic Church has a title like that. It names patrons of the missions, the people sent to the far side of the world, and it picks Francis Xavier, who sailed across oceans to preach. Fair enough. Then, beside him, it names a nun who never set foot outside her convent after she entered. Why her?
screen: `A TITLE THAT DOESN'T FIT.` → `FRANCIS XAVIER, ACROSS OCEANS.` → `AND A NUN WHO NEVER LEFT.`

segments.voice: The answer is in Manuscript B. Thérèse admits she wanted every vocation at once: priest, apostle, martyr, missionary, preaching everywhere, from the beginning of the world to its end. She knew it sounded absurd. She wanted it anyway. So she opened Saint Paul. The Church is a body with many members, he writes, and she couldn't find herself in any of them. Then he goes on, in the Douay-Rheims: "And I shew unto you yet a more excellent way." The way is charity. And there she found her place: in the heart of the Church, her mother, she would be love. Then she'd be everything. A heart doesn't travel. It sends life to every part of the body. That's the puzzle solved: the Church named her a patron of the missions because her love and prayer went where she couldn't. The second title is just as odd. Pope John Paul the Second declared her a Doctor of the Church, a teacher for everyone, in a letter that opens with the Latin for the science of divine love. No lecture hall, no long treatise. A notebook, letters, poems. Here's one to tell a friend tonight: one of the Church's official teachers did her learning in a small convent she never left.
screen: `EVERY VOCATION AT ONCE.` · `A MORE EXCELLENT WAY.` · `IN THE HEART, I WILL BE LOVE.` · `PATRON AND DOCTOR.` · then, large: `A DOCTOR WHO NEVER LEFT.`

segments.voice: Send a short message to someone far from you who's doing hard work you can't help with in person: a nurse on nights, a friend abroad, a cousin in the service. Keep it to one warm line. If you pray, you can pray for missionaries everywhere as it sends.
Patron and Doctor. Two titles the Church gave a nun who never left her convent: patron of the missions, and a teacher for everyone.
Your line: a doctor who never left. Love reaches where you can't go. Talk soon.

screen: `DAY 1535 COUNTS.` → `THE STORY OF A SOUL · 19 OF 20.` → `TOMORROW: THE LITTLE WAY, REALLY. IS IT EASY?`

fork.setup: your aunt is housebound with a long illness. she says she's useless now that she can't volunteer at the food pantry. what does Thérèse's story offer her?

fork.reveal: Thérèse wanted every vocation and found hers: love, in the heart of the Church. the Church made her a patron of missions without her ever leaving.
